findings.issue_text: Team authorization requires a user to be both an admin and an owner (`&&`), incorrectly denying team admins who are not owners despite the intended “admin or owner” policy.
The database is updated before the external calendar update; if `updateCalendarAttendees` fails, new attendees remain persisted and Cal.com becomes inconsistent with the calendar provider.

The API schema does not enforce unique guest addresses, allowing non-UI callers to submit duplicates that can create duplicate attendee records/invitations or fail `createMany` depending on database constraints.

Notification classification uses the original `guests` input rather than `uniqueGuests`, causing an existing attendee to receive a new-booking confirmation instead of a “guests added” update when a request includes both existing and new addresses.

goldens.comment: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.

The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.

The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.

uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The database is updated before the external calendar update; if `updateCalendarAttendees` fails, new attendees remain persisted and Cal.com becomes inconsistent with the calendar provider.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at addGuests.handler.ts, the code first updates the database with `prisma.booking.update` (around line 85-100) to add new attendees, then later calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` (around line 155). If the calendar update fails, the database already has the new attendees persisted, but the external calendar provider won't have them. This creates an inconsistency between Cal.com's database and the external calendar. The code doesn't wrap these operations in a transaction or have rollback logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Notification classification uses the original `guests` input rather than `uniqueGuests`, causing an existing attendee to receive a new-booking confirmation instead of a “guests added” update when a request includes both existing and new addresses.

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, the code filters guests to create `uniqueGuests` (removing existing attendees), but at the end calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` with the original `guests` array instead of `uniqueGuests`. In email-manager.ts, `sendAddGuestsEmails` uses `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` to decide whether to send AttendeeScheduledEmail (new booking confirmation) or AttendeeAddGuestsEmail (guests added update). If the original `guests` array contains an email that was already an attendee (filtered out in uniqueGuests), that existing attendee would incorrectly receive a new-booking confirmation email instead of the guests-added notification.
